name: Hudson Bay Regional Park, Ruby Lake Recreation Site
note: Hudson Bay Regional Park's small campground at Ruby Lake, a former provincial recreation site 15 km north of Hudson Bay: a wooded loop at the south end of the park's beach, boat-launch and ball-diamond grounds, beside a cottage subdivision. The park also sells seasonal camping here and does not say how many of the sites go by the season. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: townofhudsonbay.com/ruby-lake/ ('The Ruby Lake Recreation site was added to the Hudson Bay Regional Park in 2002 ... Camping consists of 2-30amp sites, 2-15amp sites, and 5 unserviced sites, fees are collected and due to Hudson Bay Regional Park'; 'Camping reservations are taken all year by phone, fax, or email'; 'Seasonal Camping at RUBY LAKE SITES- $500.00') + townofhudsonbay.com/camping/ (per-day 30 A C$35 / 15 A C$30 / non-electric C$25 'All season') + the operator's July 2026 map Hudson-Bay-Ruby-Lake-Site.pdf (13 numbered sites on one loop: 10 and 12 15 A, 11 and 13 30 A, 1-9 NS; washroom, water taps) + saskregionalparks.ca/park/hudson-bay/ (Hudson Bay Regional Park 'includes the main campground south of Hudson Bay as well as Ruby Lake'; washrooms and showers 'at both locations'; season May 10 - September 30) + SRPA 2026 guide (accredited; 'Hudson Bay - Ruby Lake -Hwy #9 N 9 km, rural road E 1.5 km N 3 km'; 'Reservations: Accepted by phone, fax & email') + the town's Ruby Lake campsite photo (a ~25-ft travel trailer and pickup on a wooded site), read 2026-11-19 -> real public campground run by a Regional Park Authority (Wikipedia: one of three former provincial recreation sites now in the regional park), nights sold by the day, no lots sold. Nightly share not measurable (seasonal offered, no count posted). Local: no price gate. Not in DB (nearest entry 9235, the park's south site, 14.7 km S). No Google listing for the campground: 'Ruby Lake' 4.3 (10) is the lake itself (category 'Lake'). (phase-7 SK lead 7, found p3-528) --Claude
waterfront_evidence: Esri World Imagery z17 (satz.py, rendered; z18 'Map data not yet available', export endpoint 500) viewed 2026-11-19 at 52.9595,-102.3515, matched to the operator's July 2026 Ruby Lake map (site loop in the woods at the south end of the grounds, lake to the west and north-west behind forest, beach and boat launch further north): the loop's nearest pads are ~170 m from Ruby Lake's shore to the north-west and ~200 m to the west, with two belts of mature forest and an open meadow strip between; the town's campsite photo shows only trees around the sites. No site within ~50 m of the water and no sightline -> not waterfront. --Claude

fees.note: Non-electric C$25 a night, 15-amp C$30, 30-amp C$35; monthly 25% less; seasonal camping at Ruby Lake C$500 plus power at C$50 a month. Park entry C$10 a day unless the camper has a seasonal regional park pass.

flags: LONG-STAY (local, unmeasured): seasonal camping is sold at Ruby Lake (C$500 + C$50/month power) but no count of seasonal sites is posted, so the nightly share can't be measured without a call. Imagery shows a few trailers parked on the loop's east side (could be seasonals). Nightly per-day rates are posted for all classes and reservations are taken all year; no wording discourages nightly guests.
Site count conflict: the town text says 9 sites (2 x 30 A, 2 x 15 A, 5 unserviced); the July 2026 operator map numbers 13 (4 electric + 9 'NS'). sites.count 13 follows the newer map.

Water/sewer hookups and dump left out: the town's 'Water Hook Ups / No Sewer (Sewer Dump $10)' lines don't say which site they cover; the map shows no dump at Ruby Lake (the park's dump is at the south site, 9235). Flush toilets left out (only 'washrooms' and 'toilets').
23-ft fit: no posted length limit; the town's Ruby Lake campsite photo shows a ~25-ft travel trailer with a pickup on a site, and the loop is an open gravel road.
Google: no listing for the campground; 'Ruby Lake' 4.3 (10) is the lake (one review mentions bringing a trailer). The regional park's own listing 4.8 (35) is pinned at the south site.
Pin placed on the site loop from imagery (Wikipedia/NRCan point 52.9601,-102.3491 is ~200 m NE, by the access road).
